source: Directive tables of the Bareos 25.1.2 Director as carried by odir (crates/odir/src/commands/show_items.rs) plus Onesimus extensions (crates/odir/src/config_check.rs EXTENSIONS)
description: A Client resource describes a File Daemon the Director backs up: where to reach it, how to authenticate, and limits and quotas for its jobs.

examples.title: A typical Linux client
A client behind NAT that connects to the Director
examples.config:
Client {
  Name = laptop-fd
  Address = laptop.example.com
  Password = "laptop-secret"
  Connection From Director To Client = no
  Connection From Client To Director = yes
}

directives.name: Name
directives.description: Name of the client as jobs, the catalog and the job logs know it. Renaming it starts a new history in the catalog, since jobs are stored by client.

examples.console: configure add client name=web-fd address=web.example.com password=client-secret

directives.name: Description
directives.description: Free text describing the client.

directives.name: Protocol
directives.description: Protocol to talk to the client: Native (the Bareos File Daemon) or one of the NDMP versions for NAS filers.

directives.name: Auth Type
directives.description: Authentication for NDMP clients: None, Clear or MD5. Native clients ignore it.

directives.name: Address
directives.description: Host name or IP address of the File Daemon. Required, since the Director connects to it (unless Connection From Client To Director is used).

directives.name: Lan Address
directives.description: Address used instead of Address when the Storage Daemon connects to the File Daemon in passive mode, for setups where storage and client share a LAN that the Director does not see.

directives.name: Port
directives.description: TCP port of the File Daemon.

directives.name: Username
directives.description: User name for NDMP authentication.

directives.name: Password
directives.description: Password shared with the File Daemon's Director resource; with TLS-PSK it is also the TLS key. Both sides must have the same value.

directives.name: Catalog
directives.description: Catalog the jobs of this client are stored in, for installations with several catalogs.

directives.name: Passive
directives.description: Passive mode: the Storage Daemon connects to the File Daemon instead of the other way round. Useful when the client may not open connections, for example behind a firewall.

directives.name: Connection From Director To Client
directives.description: The Director opens the connection to the File Daemon (the normal case).

directives.name: Connection From Client To Director
directives.description: The File Daemon connects to the Director and keeps the connection open, so a client behind NAT or a firewall can be backed up. Needs the matching setting in the File Daemon. With Run On Incoming Connect Interval a job can start when the client connects.

directives.name: Enabled
directives.description: A disabled client is not backed up by scheduled jobs; enable client and disable client change it at run time.

directives.name: Hard Quota
directives.description: Upper limit for the data of this client; a backup that would go beyond it fails. 0 means no limit. Sizes take the suffixes k, m, g, t (powers of 1024) or kb, mb, gb, tb (powers of 1000).

directives.name: Soft Quota
directives.description: Soft limit for the data of this client: beyond it a warning is written, and after the Soft Quota Grace Period jobs fail. Sizes take the suffixes k, m, g, t (powers of 1024) or kb, mb, gb, tb (powers of 1000).

directives.name: Soft Quota Grace Period
directives.description: How long the soft quota may be exceeded before jobs fail. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

directives.name: Strict Quotas
directives.description: When the soft quota grace period has run out: yes makes the soft quota a hard limit; no lets jobs run up to the hard quota.

directives.name: Quota Include Failed Jobs
directives.description: Count the data of failed jobs into the quota.

directives.name: File Retention
directives.description: Deprecated in Bareos 25: how long file records of this client's jobs are kept. Set retention in the Pool instead. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

directives.name: Job Retention
directives.description: Deprecated in Bareos 25: how long job records of this client are kept. Set retention in the Pool instead. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

directives.name: Heartbeat Interval
directives.description: Interval of keep-alive packets to the File Daemon. 0 switches it off. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

directives.name: Auto Prune
directives.description: Deprecated in Bareos 25: prune this client's jobs and files after each job.

directives.name: Maximum Concurrent Jobs
directives.description: How many jobs may run on this client at the same time; further jobs wait. Raise it when several jobs (for example per file system) back up the same host.

directives.name: Maximum Bandwidth Per Job
directives.description: Limits the bandwidth of each job of this client. Speeds take the suffixes k/s, m/s (powers of 1024) or kb/s, mb/s (powers of 1000); a plain number means bytes per second.

directives.name: NDMP Log Level
directives.description: Detail of NDMP messages of this client, 0 to 9.

directives.name: NDMP Block Size
directives.description: Block size of NDMP backups. Sizes take the suffixes k, m, g, t (powers of 1024) or kb, mb, gb, tb (powers of 1000).

directives.name: NDMP Use LMDB
directives.description: Keep the NDMP file history in an LMDB database during the job instead of in memory, for filers with many files.

directives.name: TLS Authenticate
directives.description: Use TLS only to authenticate the peer and switch back to an unencrypted connection afterwards. The data then travels in clear text, so this is meant for networks that are protected otherwise. Bareos' default TLS-PSK setup does not need it.

directives.name: TLS Enable
directives.description: Enable TLS for this connection. Since Bareos 18.2 TLS is on by default and uses TLS-PSK with the password of the resource, so no certificates are needed; set it to no only for peers that cannot speak TLS.

directives.name: TLS Require
directives.description: Refuse connections that do not use TLS. With the default (yes) a peer without TLS cannot connect; set it to no only during a migration from very old clients.

directives.name: TLS Cipher List
directives.description: OpenSSL cipher list for TLS 1.2 and older, colon separated. Leave it empty to use the OpenSSL defaults; restrict it only when a security policy demands specific ciphers.

directives.name: TLS Cipher Suites
directives.description: OpenSSL cipher suites for TLS 1.3, colon separated. Empty means the OpenSSL defaults.

directives.name: TLS DH File
directives.description: PEM file with Diffie-Hellman parameters for the DH key exchange of TLS 1.2. Without it, ephemeral DH ciphers are not offered; ECDHE and PSK ciphers do not need it.

directives.name: TLS Protocol
directives.description: Restricts the TLS protocol versions in OpenSSL syntax, for example to forbid old versions. Empty means the OpenSSL default.

directives.name: TLS Verify Peer
directives.description: With certificate based TLS: check the peer's certificate against the CA and, for a server, against TLS Allowed CN. It has no effect with TLS-PSK.

directives.name: TLS Ca Certificate File
directives.description: PEM file with the CA certificates used to verify the peer's certificate. Needed for certificate based TLS when TLS Verify Peer is on (or use TLS CA Certificate Dir).

directives.name: TLS Ca Certificate Dir
directives.description: Directory of hashed CA certificates (as made by openssl rehash), an alternative to TLS CA Certificate File.

directives.name: TLS Certificate Revocation List
directives.description: PEM file with a certificate revocation list; certificates on it are refused.

directives.name: TLS Certificate
directives.description: PEM file with the own certificate for certificate based TLS. Goes together with TLS Key.

directives.name: TLS Key
directives.description: PEM file with the private key of TLS Certificate. Keep it readable for the daemon user only.

directives.name: TLS Allowed CN
directives.description: Common names a peer certificate may carry; others are refused when TLS Verify Peer is on. Repeat the directive for several names.
